## Context
Cut the next minor release, 0.11.0, from reviewed main using docs/releasing.md. The current package and latest tag are 0.10.1/v0.10.1. PyPI is immutable; publication must use the dispatch-from-main workflow and its required pypi environment approval. The release date is 2026-08-06. Closed ticket 5ac8-96d1-4691-49a5 is the 0.10.1 release precedent, not active duplicate work.

Post-publication rebar-debug investigation proved that docs/releasing.md currently prescribes the wrong provenance verifier: gh attestation verify queries GitHub Artifact Attestations for SLSA provenance, while pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish uploads a PEP 740 publish/v1 bundle to PyPI. The observed CLI surface is `uvx pypi-attestations verify pypi PYPI_FILE --repository REPOSITORY`; running it against the downloaded 0.11.0 wheel and https://github.com/navapbc/rebar returned OK. Follow-up bug 13b4-c597-200b-4e31 owns the runbook and workflow-comment correction.

## Plan
- Work in a fresh worktree based on current origin/main and confirm release prerequisites, identity, recent Gerrit history/rights, and channel state.
- Bump pyproject.toml and every version in server.json to 0.11.0; regenerate uv.lock so the root project version remains locked at 0.11.0; generate and hand-curate the 0.11.0 CHANGELOG section dated 2026-08-06 and its compare links.
- Run version-lockstep and proportional release preflight: release-specific tests/guards, lock-currentness, lint, typecheck, full tests, build, and twine checks.
- Commit with DCO, Change-Id, and rebar-ticket trailer; send through Gerrit and wait for LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 with no unresolved comments, then Submit.
- After the bump lands on main, dispatch release.yml from main with version=0.11.0 and obtain the required pypi environment approval; monitor the entire workflow to a terminal result.
- Verify PyPI 0.11.0 plus PEP 740 provenance, the v0.11.0 GitHub tag/release and artifacts, MCP Registry 0.11.0, and the Homebrew tap bump (trigger autobump if useful).
- Install nava-rebar[mcp]==0.11.0 from PyPI in the distribution-channel environment and run the packaged post-publication probe.
- Record receipts and results on this ticket, then close it only after all acceptance criteria are met.

## File impact
- pyproject.toml — package version bump
- server.json — MCP manifest/package version bump
- uv.lock — root package version lockstep with pyproject.toml
- CHANGELOG.md — curated 0.11.0 release notes and compare links

## Rollback / failure policy
Before publish, stop on any failed guard, review, or CI vote and remediate through a new Gerrit patchset. After publish, PyPI cannot be replaced: if the artifact is bad, yank 0.11.0, de-list its GitHub Release, and cut a fixed patch version; do not overwrite artifacts or retag published content.
